title: Combining heart rate variability and accelerometer features for stress detection in free-living conditions

record.title: Combining heart rate variability and accelerometer features for stress detection in free-living conditions
record.abstract: Continuous stress monitoring in everyday life has attracted growing interest as a tool for preventive mental health management, yet most validated methods require laboratory-controlled conditions. This paper investigates a multimodal approach that fuses heart rate variability (HRV) indices derived from a chest-worn ECG patch with accelerometer-based activity features to infer subjective stress levels in free-living adults. Thirty-six participants wore the sensor system continuously for five days while self-reporting stress events via a smartphone application. A total of 41 time-domain, frequency-domain, and nonlinear HRV features were extracted over non-overlapping five-minute windows and combined with six activity context features capturing posture and movement intensity. A random forest classifier trained with leave-one-day-out cross-validation achieved a binary stress/non-stress accuracy of 76.4%, improving by 8.3 percentage points over HRV-only baselines. Analysis of feature importance revealed that low-frequency HRV power and accelerometer-derived posture class were the two most discriminative predictors. The study highlights that activity context is an important confound in wearable stress detection and should be accounted for in algorithm design.
